subject: Dedicated capacity post-call recap PulseMed
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@pulsemed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-03-07T15:15:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity post-call recap PulseMed

Hi Emma / Amit,

Thanks for taking the time earlier today appreciate the walkthrough of PulseMed's current inference workload and constraints. Per our call, this is a short recap of the pain points, goals, and proposed next steps so we have a mutual action plan.

Summary of pain points we heard:
- High token volume (real-time clinical triage + batch nightly enrichment) causing unpredictable latency and outsized cloud spend.
- Data residency / isolation requirements for PHI-like metadata you need a dedicated environment rather than multi-tenant endpoints.
- Spiky traffic during patient intake windows; current autoscaling is slow and leading to dropped requests.

Goals you stated:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) with strict isolation for the sensitive inference pipeline.
- P95 tail latency <= 150ms for the interactive triage path at steady-state load.
- Predictable monthly committed spend with burst capacity for peak windows.
- SOC2 / audit evidence and an ability to control key rotation (KMS).

Our recommended config (high level):
- Redwood Dedicated: reserved pool of 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs with a separate VPC/private deployment for data isolation.
- Autoscaling policy: target-backed scaling with pre-warmed burst slots and a fast scale-up path to handle intake spikes.
- Optimizations: model quantization profile + KV prefix caching for the triage prompt to reduce per-token cost and hit P95 target.
- SLAs: 99.9% uptime target with SLOs for queueing latency; we will validate P95 in a 2-week soak with representative traffic.

Attachments: attached a preliminary estimate and a capacity map (pulsemed-dedicated-estimate.pdf, pulsemed-map.xlsx) for your review. Also attaching a SOC2 summary that we referenced.

Next steps (action items):
1) PulseMed: share sample traffic profile (1-2 representative 24h traces) and any compliance checklist specifics (PHI handling requirements) Amit to share by 2027-03-10.
2) Redwood: spin up a scoped Dedicated config estimate + a draft SOW and calendar a technical deep dive with Marissa (solutions) to validate autoscaling and networking I’ll follow up with proposed times.
3) Both: align on committed capacity and billing cadence after technical validation (target decision by 2027-03-24).

If that all looks right, I’ll send the SOW/estimate and a calendar invite for the tech deep dive.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- PHI handling: we need customer-managed KMS and logs retention for 1 year I’ll attach the compliance checklist.
- On burst capacity: we want at least a 2x burst above committed baseline during scheduled intake hours.

Can Marissa and Rachel join the technical call next week? Prefer Wed or Thu morning PST.
